title: Ottomans: more than one city
hook: Did a new capital erase the empire’s other centers?

knows: Events happen in places and at different times.

objective: Constantinople became an imperial capital, but the empire remained a network of places.

claims.text: Early 1300s: Anatolia. A frontier principality expands.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/the-art-of-the-ottomans-before-1600 — Early principality, 1453, 1517 and provincial production centers

claims.text: 1453: New capital. Ottoman forces capture Constantinople.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/the-art-of-the-ottomans-before-1600 — Early principality, 1453, 1517 and provincial production centers

claims.text: 1517: Egypt. The conquest of Mamluk lands extends rule.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/the-art-of-the-ottomans-before-1600 — Early principality, 1453, 1517 and provincial production centers

claims.text: 1500s: Many centers. Provincial cities remain artistic production centers.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/the-art-of-the-ottomans-before-1600 — Early principality, 1453, 1517 and provincial production centers

claims.text: Constantinople became an imperial capital, but the empire remained a network of places. Expansion incorporated Syria and Egypt, while cities such as Bursa, Cairo and Baghdad contributed distinct artistic industries. A capital’s prominence does not mean all production moved there.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/the-art-of-the-ottomans-before-1600 — Early principality, 1453, 1517 and provincial production centers

recall.question: After 1453, was imperial activity confined to the capital?
recall.why: Constantinople became an imperial capital, but the empire remained a network of places. Expansion incorporated Syria and Egypt, while cities such as Bursa, Cairo and Baghdad contributed distinct artistic industries. A capital’s prominence does not mean all production moved there.
